exercises.prompt: Implement sortAsc(arr) so it returns a new array with arr's numbers in ascending order. Do not modify the original array — sort a copy. An empty array returns an empty array.
hints: sort orders an array, but with no comparator it sorts by text, so numbers need one — and it changes the array in place, so work on a copy.
Spread into a fresh array first with [...arr], then sort that; the numeric comparator is (a, b) => a - b.
return [...arr].sort((a, b) => a - b) — the copy protects the caller's array and a - b orders numbers ascending.

exercises.prompt: Implement sortDesc(arr) so it returns a new array with arr's numbers in descending order (largest first), without modifying the original. An empty array returns an empty array.
hints: Descending is the same sort with the comparison reversed.
Swap the operands: (a, b) => b - a puts larger numbers first.
return [...arr].sort((a, b) => b - a) — still sorting a copy so the original is untouched.

exercises.prompt: Implement sortByLength(arr), where arr is an array of strings, so it returns a new array ordered from shortest to longest by string length, without modifying the original. Strings of equal length keep their original relative order. An empty array returns an empty array.
hints: Sort by a derived value — each string's length — rather than by the strings themselves.
Compare the lengths in the comparator: (a, b) => a.length - b.length.
return [...arr].sort((a, b) => a.length - b.length); equal-length strings stay in their original order because sort is stable.

exercises.prompt: Implement sortByAbs(arr) so it returns a new array with arr's numbers ordered by absolute value (distance from zero), smallest distance first, without modifying the original. So [-3, 1, -2] becomes [1, -2, -3]. An empty array returns an empty array.
hints: Order by a computed key again — this time each number's absolute value, its distance from zero.
Math.abs(x) drops the sign; compare those in the comparator: (a, b) => Math.abs(a) - Math.abs(b).
return [...arr].sort((a, b) => Math.abs(a) - Math.abs(b)) — note -2 sorts before -3 because 2 < 3.

exercises.prompt: Implement kSmallest(arr, k) so it returns a new array of the k smallest numbers in arr, in ascending order. If k is 0 the result is empty; if k is larger than arr.length, return all of arr sorted. Do not modify the original array.
hints: Two steps: put the numbers in ascending order, then take the first k of them.
Sort a copy with (a, b) => a - b, then slice(0, k) keeps the first k — and slice is safe when k is 0 or larger than the array.
